facts.rationale: Replaces generalized state labels with exact branches, including unknown-state polling and exceptional return behavior.
facts.value: With interrupts disabled, initializes reboot metadata, installs a cleared stack context, initializes DVD handling and starts asynchronous reset preparation. A false DVDCheckDisk result calls __OSDoHotReset; if it returns, execution continues. The routine masks 0xFFFFFFE0, unmasks 0x400 and enables interrupts. Each ReadApploader waits while Prepared is FALSE, submits a read, and polls its command block: 0 completes, 1 and default values continue waiting, and -1 or 2–11 call __OSDoHotReset and continue polling if it returns. Submission results are unchecked and there is no timeout. Prepared is not cleared on entry. Two completed reads lead to cache invalidation and the intended terminal Run handoff.

evidence.why: Complete unit establishes initialization, absence of clearing, polling branches and success sequence.

facts.rationale: Preserves synchronization knowledge while documenting numeric-state ambiguity and potentially indefinite waits.
facts.value: The volatile Prepared latch is statically zero-initialized, set TRUE unconditionally by Callback, and never cleared in this unit. ReadApploader waits on that latch before each submission, then returns only on command state 0. State 1 and unlisted values keep polling; -1 and 2–11 invoke hot reset and resume polling if it returns. There is no timeout or submission-result check. A failed disc check also invokes hot reset, with subsequent code still present if it returns. Two completed reads advance to cache invalidation and execution of the loaded reboot payload.
